card.subject: accountancy
card.front: The Partnership Act does not require that the agreement must be in ____.
card.back: The Partnership Act does not require that the agreement must be in writing.
card.quote: The Partnership Act does not require that the agreement must be in writing.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: The clauses of partnership deed can be altered with the ____ of all the partners.
card.back: The clauses of partnership deed can be altered with the consent of all the partners.
card.quote: The clauses of partnership deed can be altered with the consent of all the partners.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Which Act's provisions apply to a partnership matter the deed has no express agreement on?
card.back: However, if there is no express agreement on certain matters, the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 shall apply.
card.quote: However, if there is no express agreement on certain matters, the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 shall apply.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Can a partner claim interest on capital as a matter of right?
card.back: No partner is entitled to claim any interest on the amount of capital contributed by him in the firm as a matter of right.
card.quote: No partner is entitled to claim any interest on the amount of capital contributed by him in the firm as a matter of right.

source.section: 1.2.1 Provisions of Partnership Act Relevant for Accounting

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: At what rate is interest on a partner’s loan payable if the deed is silent?
card.back: If any partner has advanced loan to the firm for the purpose of business, he/she shall be entitled to get an interest on the loan amount at the rate of 6 per cent per annum.
card.quote: If any partner has advanced loan to the firm for the purpose of business, he/she shall be entitled to get an interest on the loan amount at the rate of 6 per cent per annum.

source.section: 1.2.1 Provisions of Partnership Act Relevant for Accounting

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: According to the Partnership Act, what is the position when the deed is silent?
card.back:
the partners share profits equally
no partner is entitled to remuneration
no interest on capital is allowed
no interest on drawings is charged
he is entitled to interest on such amount @ 6% per annum
card.quote: According to the Partnership Act, the partners share profits equally, no partner is entitled to remuneration, no interest on capital is allowed and no interest on drawings is charged. However, if any partner has given some loan to the firm, he is entitled to interest on such amount @ 6% per annum.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: What is the fixed capital method?
card.back: Under the fixed capital method, the capitals of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement among the partners.
card.quote: Under the fixed capital method, the capitals of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement among the partners.

source.section: 1.4 Maintenance of Capital Accounts of Partners

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Fixed capital method: where do the capital and current account balances appear in the balance sheet?
card.back: While the partners’ capital accounts shall always appear on the liabilities side in the balance sheet, the partners’ current account’s balance shall be shown on the liabilities side, if they have credit balance and on the assets side, if they have debit balance.
card.quote: While the partners’ capital accounts shall always appear on the liabilities side in the balance sheet, the partners’ current account’s balance shall be shown on the liabilities side, if they have credit balance and on the assets side, if they have debit balance.

source.section: 1.4 Maintenance of Capital Accounts of Partners

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: What is the fluctuating capital method?
card.back: Under the fluctuating capital method, only one account, i.e. capital account is maintained for each partner.
card.quote: Under the fluctuating capital method, only one account, i.e. capital account is maintained for each partner.

source.section: 1.4 Maintenance of Capital Accounts of Partners

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Fixed vs Fluctuating capital: the difference on items related to the deed (drawings, salary, interest on capital).
card.back:
Fixed Capital
Drawings, salary, interest on capital, etc. are posted (transfered) in the current accounts and not in the capital accounts.
Fluctuating Capital
All adjustments for drawings, salary, interest on capital, etc., are posted (transfered) in the capital accounts.
card.quote: Fixed Capital Fluctuating Capital (i) Number of accounts (ii) Items related to deed (iii) Fixed balance (iv) Credit balance Under this method, two separate accounts are maintained for each partner viz., ‘capital account’ and ‘current account’. Drawings, salary,interest on capital,etc. are posted (transfered) in the current accounts and not in the capital accounts. The capital account balance remain unchanged unless there is addition to or withdrawal of capital. The capital accounts always show a credit balance. Each partner has one account, i.e. capital account, under this method All adjustments for drawings, salary interest on capital, etc., are posted (transfered) in the capital accounts,

source.section: 1.4.1 Distinction between Fixed and Fluctuating Capital Accounts
